title: Adopt Verus for the Python-facing Rust core
description:
Context
This repository is a uv-managed Maturin mixed project. The public Python API is backed by a private PyO3 module. The goal is to add a pure Rust core verified with Verus without changing the package manager, build backend, minimum Python version, distribution name, import package, or private-extension topology.

Deliverables
- Verus-verify the existing checked add operation.
- Add and verify checked_sum, lower_bound, and first-match binary_search.
- Keep PyO3 as a thin, explicitly unverified adapter.
- Provide reproducible local and CI proof commands.
- Test Python contracts, Rust runtime behavior, packages, and error mapping.
- Document exactly what Verus proves and the trusted computing base.

Proof policy
Safe core entry points reachable from Python must not expose unchecked requires clauses. Project-authored proof code must contain no assume, admitted axiom, or undocumented external specification. Verification is not a performance claim and does not replace tests, lint, typing, coverage, or package checks.

Design
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-verus-verified-python-rust-design.md

## Success Criteria

- The pinned full Verus command reports zero errors for the entire verified core.
- add, checked_sum, lower_bound, and binary_search meet their approved Python and mathematical contracts.
- Unsorted search input is rejected by an executable core check and maps to ValueError.
- Prefix overflow and Python integer conversion failures map to OverflowError as documented.
- Existing and new Make targets, normal Cargo checks, Python checks, coverage, packaging, and isolated-wheel smoke tests pass.
- CI runs the same full proof command used locally.
- Documentation identifies all assumptions, external specifications, unverified layers, tool versions, supported platforms, and known limits.
- No benchmark, speed claim, fallback, or package/build migration is introduced.

title: Pin and validate the Verus toolchain
description:
Scope
Choose one official Verus release and record the compatible Rust toolchain, cargo-verus binary, Z3 supplied by or required by that release, and vstd dependency revision. Validate the choice with a minimal library proof and a normal Cargo build.

Implementation notes
- Use official release artifacts and checksums or another immutable source.
- Do not use a moving latest URL, branch, or unpinned git dependency in CI.
- Record supported host platforms and the installation command for local developers.
- Confirm how cargo verus locates the pinned toolchain and vstd.
- Keep stable Rust available for the existing PyO3, Clippy, test, and coverage paths unless the pinned Verus release explicitly requires a coordinated change.

Evidence
Capture version output and the commands needed to reproduce the spike. Record any unsupported host or architecture rather than claiming support.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A specific Verus release, Rust toolchain, vstd revision, and installation source are recorded.
- verus --version and cargo verus --help succeed in a clean documented setup.
- A minimal opted-in library verifies with zero errors.
- The same annotated library builds with normal Cargo.
- The plan names Linux CI support and any untested platforms.
- No project package metadata or public Python API changes are made in this task.

title: Run the pinned Verus proof gate in CI
description:
Scope
Add a GitHub Actions job that installs the exact Verus release selected by the toolchain bead and invokes the Makefile full-proof target.

Requirements
Use immutable release identifiers and verify downloaded artifacts when the release process supplies checksums. Keep workflow permissions minimal. Cache only paths whose keys include the pinned Verus, Rust, vstd, Cargo.lock, and relevant source inputs. Do not maintain a separate CI-only verifier command.

The proof job may run independently of Python tests, but package publication or the final package job must not pass when verification fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- CI installs the pinned Verus toolchain reproducibly on Ubuntu.
- CI runs the Makefile full-proof target, not a duplicated command list.
- A proof failure makes the workflow fail.
- Cache keys cannot reuse proof artifacts across incompatible toolchain or lockfile changes.
- Existing Python 3.11 and 3.13 jobs, Rust checks, coverage, and package checks remain present.
- Workflow documentation names platforms not exercised by CI.

title: Document Verus usage and verify packaged artifacts

State that Verus proves the pure core and that runtime tests cover PyO3 and Python behavior. Link to AGENTS.md and the official Verus tutorial.

Packaging
Ensure wheel and source distribution builds include the workspace core sources needed for reproducible builds. Extend the isolated-wheel smoke test to call all functions from outside the checkout and assert the compiled native module is loaded.

title: Complete the proof, package, and trust-boundary audit
description:
Scope
Run the complete local command surface from a clean checkout-equivalent state and audit every verification claim before closing the epic.

Audit checklist
- Record Verus, cargo-verus, vstd, Z3, Rust, Cargo, Python, uv, Maturin, and PyO3 versions.
- Run the full proof and API safety check.
- Inspect project proof sources for assume, axioms, external_body, external, assume_specification, and manual triggers.
- Match every trusted item to documentation and a runtime test where applicable.
- Run lint, typing, Rust and Python tests, coverage, repeated package builds, archive inspection, and isolated-wheel smoke tests.
- Compare CI commands with Make targets.
- Report operating systems, architectures, and Python versions not exercised.

Do not close on partial evidence or by raising thresholds and limits until failures disappear.

## Acceptance Criteria

- make check and the documented full Verus target pass from the recorded environment.
- Verus reports zero errors for every opted-in core crate.
- All external assumptions and trusted components are listed and justified.
- No project-authored assume, admitted axiom, or undocumented external specification remains.
- Public core APIs reachable from Python pass the safe-API review and have no unchecked preconditions.
- Wheel and source distribution checks pass outside the checkout.
- CI is green using the same Make targets.
- The handoff reports exact proof scope and untested platforms without speed or whole-stack verification claims.

title: Create the private Verus-verified core crate
description:
Scope
Turn the Rust portion into a small Cargo workspace while leaving the root package as the Maturin cdylib. Add a private pure-Rust library crate for Verus-verified algorithms and make the root PyO3 crate depend on it.

Implementation notes
- Keep the root Cargo package, library name _native, PyO3 features, Maturin module name, and Python source layout unchanged.
- Add vstd and package.metadata.verus only to the verified core.
- Import vstd::prelude and establish the chosen verus macro or attribute convention.
- Keep PyO3, Python exception types, module registration, I/O, and business-domain concerns out of the core.
- Update Cargo.lock and package exclusion rules.
- Confirm that the Maturin source distribution includes every file needed to build the workspace crate from an archive.
- Add the cfg(verus_only) lint declaration required by current Rust.

Evidence
Use a placeholder or minimal verified function only to prove the topology. Algorithm work belongs to later beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- cargo metadata shows the root extension crate and one private verified-core member.
- cargo verus verify can select and verify the core crate.
- cargo build, cargo test, cargo clippy, and Maturin development build still work.
- The core has no PyO3 or Python dependency.
- Cargo.lock is updated and checked in.
- A built source distribution contains the core manifest and sources and can build outside the checkout.
- Existing Python add behavior remains unchanged.

title: Specify and verify checked add
description:
Scope
Move the existing i64 checked-add logic into the verified core and give it a total, precondition-free contract. Preserve the existing PyO3 wrapper behavior until the adapter bead rewires it.

Contract
For any a and b representable as i64, success returns their mathematical sum exactly when that sum fits in i64. Otherwise the core returns its arithmetic-overflow error. The implementation must not panic or wrap.

Proof notes
Specify the mathematical result with int. Relate Some or Ok to the exact sum and the failure variant to a sum outside i64 bounds. Avoid external specifications if vstd already specifies checked_add. If an external specification is unavoidable, document and runtime-test it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The public core add function has no requires clause.
- Verus proves exact successful addition and both overflow directions with zero errors.
- Rust tests cover positive, negative, zero, i64 boundaries, upper overflow, and lower overflow.
- The executable implementation uses checked arithmetic and contains no expected-failure panic.
- Project-authored proof code adds no assume, admitted axiom, or undocumented external specification.
- Existing Python add tests still pass after later adapter wiring.
acceptance_criteria:
- The public core add function has no requires clause.

title: Specify and verify checked_sum prefix semantics
description:
Scope
Add a verified, precondition-free checked_sum over an executable sequence of i64 values.

Contract
Fold left to right from zero. Return the exact accumulated sum when every mathematical prefix sum fits in i64. Return arithmetic overflow at the first prefix that falls outside the i64 range, even if later values could make the final mathematical total fit again. Empty input returns zero.

Proof notes
Use a mathematical Seq view and a specification for prefix sums. Maintain loop invariants relating the executable accumulator and index to the mathematical prefix. Prove all indexing and arithmetic bounds. Keep the failure contract precise enough to distinguish prefix overflow from a final-total-only policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- checked_sum is callable safely for every representable input sequence and has no requires clause.
- Verus proves empty, success, and prefix-overflow result conditions with zero errors.
- The loop has explicit index, accumulator, sequence-view, and termination invariants.
- Rust tests cover empty input, mixed signs, i64 boundaries, positive and negative prefix overflow, and a later-cancellation case that still errors.
- The implementation does not panic, wrap, or allocate ghost state at runtime.
- Project-authored proof code adds no assume or undocumented trusted specification.

- checked_sum is callable safely for every representable input sequence and has no requires clause.

title: Verify sortedness checking and lower_bound
description:
Scope
Add a precondition-free lower_bound core API for i64 sequences. The public core function must validate nondecreasing order at runtime before calling any internal helper that requires sortedness.

Contract
For sorted input, return the smallest index i such that values[i] is greater than or equal to target, or len(values) if no such element exists. For unsorted input, return a distinct domain error. Duplicate values return the first eligible index.

Proof notes
Define a mathematical sortedness predicate over the Seq view. Verify that the executable order scan establishes it. For the binary-search loop, prove low and high bounds, strict progress, all elements before the result are less than target, and all elements from the result onward are at least target. Avoid overflow in midpoint calculation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The safe public core API has no requires clause and rejects unsorted input explicitly.
- Verus proves that successful output is within 0..=len.
- Verus proves the left partition is less than target and the right partition is at least target.
- Verus proves minimality, including first position among duplicates.
- Verus proves loop termination, safe indexing, and midpoint arithmetic.
- Rust tests cover empty, singleton, before-first, after-last, present, absent, duplicates, i64 boundaries, and unsorted inputs.
- No project-authored assume or undocumented external specification is introduced.
acceptance_criteria:
- The safe public core API has no requires clause and rejects unsorted input explicitly.
- Verus proves that successful output is within 0..=len.
- Verus proves the left partition is less than target and the right partition is at least target.
- Verus proves minimality, including first position among duplicates.
- Verus proves loop termination, safe indexing, and midpoint arithmetic.
- Rust tests cover empty, singleton, before-first, after-last, present, absent, duplicates, i64 boundaries, and unsorted inputs.
- No project-authored assume or undocumented external specification is introduced.

title: Specify and verify first-match binary_search
description:
Scope
Add binary_search to the verified core by reusing the verified sortedness and lower-bound path.

Contract
For sorted input, return Some(i) exactly when target occurs, with i equal to the first matching index. Return None when no element equals target. Propagate the distinct unsorted-input domain error.

Proof notes
Use lower_bound postconditions rather than duplicating its search loop. Prove the final optional index check is in bounds before indexing. Prove None means absence across the whole sequence and Some means equality plus first-match minimality.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The safe public core API has no requires clause.
- Verus proves Some indices are in bounds, equal the target, and are the first match.
- Verus proves None means no sequence element equals the target.
- Unsorted input returns the same domain error as lower_bound.
- Rust tests cover empty, singleton, present, absent, duplicate, boundary-target, and unsorted cases.
- The implementation reuses lower_bound rather than maintaining a second search loop.
- The full core verifies with no new assumptions.
acceptance_criteria:
- The safe public core API has no requires clause.
- Verus proves Some indices are in bounds, equal the target, and are the first match.
- Verus proves None means no sequence element equals the target.
- Unsorted input returns the same domain error as lower_bound.
- Rust tests cover empty, singleton, present, absent, duplicate, boundary-target, and unsorted cases.
- The implementation reuses lower_bound rather than maintaining a second search loop.
- The full core verifies with no new assumptions.

title: Wire verified core results through thin PyO3 adapters
description:
Scope
Replace algorithm logic in the root cdylib with thin calls into the verified core. Register add, checked_sum, lower_bound, and binary_search in the private _native module.

Boundary contract
- Rust arithmetic overflow maps to PyOverflowError.
- Unsorted search input maps to PyValueError.
- PyO3 conversion failures keep their normal TypeError or OverflowError behavior.
- lower_bound returns a Python int.
- binary_search returns int or None.
- No expected failure panics.
- Python extraction, allocation, exception construction, and module registration remain explicitly unverified.

Implementation notes
Keep adapters small enough to audit. Do not duplicate algorithms in the PyO3 crate. Do not add a Python fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each native function delegates its algorithm to the verified-core crate.
- Exact error mapping matches the approved contract.
- The private module registers exactly the four supported callables.
- Out-of-range Python integers raise OverflowError and wrong argument types raise TypeError.
- Unsorted search sequences raise ValueError.
- The adapter has no duplicated checked-sum or search algorithm.
- Existing add signature, keyword behavior, and exceptions remain compatible.

- Each native function delegates its algorithm to the verified-core crate.

title: Expose and test the four-function Python API
description:
Scope
Re-export add, checked_sum, lower_bound, and binary_search from the Python package. Update __all__, the private native stub, package docs, and Python contract tests without exposing the verified-core crate as a Python module.

Tests
Cover native loading, callable surface, positional and keyword calls, empty sequences, mixed signs, bounds, prefix overflow, later cancellation, sorted search, unsorted input, duplicates, present and absent targets, invalid containers, invalid elements, missing arguments, and extra arguments.

Typing
Use Sequence[int] for accepted sequence inputs if runtime extraction supports that contract. If PyO3 accepts a narrower shape, document and type the narrower contract instead of overstating it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The package exports exactly add, checked_sum, lower_bound, and binary_search.
- _native.pyi and py.typed expose the same signatures as runtime behavior.
- Tests assert exact successful values and exact exception classes.
- Duplicate searches return the first matching index.
- lower_bound returns len(values) when target is above every element.
- checked_sum documents and tests prefix-overflow semantics.
- Tests import through the public package while also confirming the native binary loaded.
- Python coverage remains at the repository threshold.

title: Add stable Make targets for Verus verification
description:
Scope
Add a noninteractive Makefile surface for full Verus verification and any useful focused development command. Preserve every current target and keep native builds serialized.

Requirements
- Add a prerequisite check that names the exact pinned installation instructions when verus or cargo-verus is missing.
- The full target verifies every opted-in core crate and checks the API safety mode if supported by the pinned release.
- Add a proof-hygiene check for project-authored assume, admitted axioms, and unreviewed external specifications without scanning third-party vstd sources.
- Include the full proof target in check in a clear order.
- A focus target may exist for local iteration but must not satisfy CI or completion by itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

- make help lists the new verification commands.
- The full target fails on a Verus proof error and succeeds only after full core verification.
- Missing tools produce a direct pinned installation command and exit nonzero.
- The hygiene check is scoped to project-authored proof files and detects a deliberate fixture or controlled test violation.
- make check includes full verification and remains noninteractive and fail-fast.
- Existing setup, build, test, lint, typecheck, coverage, and package-check target names continue to work.
